warnings.warning: Equation 4 places hardness in an Arrhenius-like environmental exponent without a dimensionless normalization.
Equation 5 equates P times C, a force under the surrounding definitions, with an integral of G(t) over time, which is an impulse.
Equation 6 appears to add an additional time-proportional sliding factor relative to Equation 3, leaving time dimensions unresolved.
Equation 22 reuses free index i in its denominator and prints the upper limit as M instead of the 2k mixture components.
Equation 25 prints the second covariance vector with x_i rather than sample x_m.
Equation 26 sums over sample m but prints a density at generic x,y instead of x_m.
The text proposes 1<=k<=10 while Figure 9 displays a wider horizontal range; the actual candidate set is unclear.
Equation 30-31 repair detection lacks neighborhood size, calibrated threshold, labeled examples, and performance metrics.
Equation 32 changes notation from alpha/alpha_e to K/K_e and omits sample, significance, and test-result details.
Equations 34-36 reuse s as deviatoric stress and damage exponent; S, s, and m roles and units are ambiguous.
S=0.1 MPa^-1 is dimensionally incompatible with the printed (Y/S)^s damage factor under the supplied definitions.
The printed Y is about 1.96e-3 MPa, while the stated stress and elastic modulus give about 1.96e-8 MPa.
Even using printed Y, direct substitution gives damage near 1.32e-7 rather than 2.3e-9; kPa/MPa and hydrostatic-stress handling are also inconsistent.
The assigned stresses are far below the stated 20 MPa yield stress, yet a nonzero plastic strain increment is imposed without explanation.
Figure 12's concentrated duration, MPa stress axis, and cumulative-damage magnitude do not match the one-hour, kPa, and 1e-4/1e-6 text values.
The 4.89 percent validation claim lacks raw observations, sample size, error definition, uncertainty, and an independently reproducible experiment.

support_steps: Represent pointwise steps as Bernoulli events.

Compare n_up and n_down and interpret k/2.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Show an ancient worn stair as the observable object that motivates historical inference.
Map Archard wear, LiDAR, GMM, Monte Carlo, repair detection, material tests, and fatigue comparison into the task flow.
Bind the main wear, behavior, direction, probability, and fatigue symbols to meanings and units where stated.
Demonstrate a three-dimensional scan representation of stair-surface wear.
Provide source-stated wear-coefficient ranges for selected material pairs.
Show the pressure-footprint context used to motivate localized wear.
Identify Z1, Z2, and Z3 phases on a standard vertical GRF curve.
Report ascent/descent contact times and GRF extrema used in directional fitting.
Compare fitted upward and downward ground-reaction-force curves, though the colored lines lack a legend.
Show the LiDAR wear-depth surface that is integrated into total volume.
Show spatial footfall clusters that motivate a Gaussian mixture; the color scale lacks numeric ticks.
Show the wear-depth field passed to the mixture fit; the relation to the four footfall clusters needs explanation.
Compare BIC over component count for different simultaneous-user scenarios.
Show a GMM fit to the wear-depth field as the direction/crowding inference example.
Expose the Monte Carlo input, draw, force-distance, position, accumulation, and output sequence.
Compare 5, 10, 15, and 20-year three-dimensional wear surfaces and connect the critical depth to maintenance.
Compare traffic, cumulative damage, and stress over time in three panels; units and magnitudes conflict with the prose calculation.
